newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA INTERBANK MARKET RATES (CHIBOR) MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CHINA INTERBANK MARKET RATES (CHIBOR) MIXED.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wedensday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell further to 648 million yuan from a thin 685 million with the one-day contract the most actively traded.
Trading continued dull with both state banks and non-banking financial institutions traded lightly, dealers said.
The market has been hit by an oversupply of funds due to a lack of borrowers since Beijing took a series of measures between May and July to standardise the financial markets.

The measures have effectively checked irregularities on the interbank market but also left financial institutions less eager to trade -- particularly securities houses that are major borrowers on the market.
"Bank.. have an ample supply of funds but there are few borrowers," one trader said. "This depressed volume today."
Traders said rumours the central bank would soon cut bank reserve ratios had created market uncertainty for a third day, leaving institutions reluctant to trade.
The required reserve ratio, the sum Chinese banks must deposit with the central bank as a proportion of total deposits, now stands at 13 percent.
Rumours of a cut have circulated periodically since July last year, when the central bank said it was considering such a move. Officials have declined to give a timetable.
Traders said they expected interbank rates to move narrowly in slow trade in the short term on ample fund supply.
